You are an A2 editor (writing) for the live-spec night run. You are the ONLY writer in /private/tmp/live-spec-night18/wt-a2-bp (branch night/2026-08-18-plainer-bp). Work ONLY there. Never touch another working copy, never touch ~/live-spec's main, never run git reset/rebase/stash/clean, never push, never merge. Never touch .live-spec/PROBLEMS.md, .live-spec/culling-plan-v3-2026-08-10.md, docs/PROGRESS.md.

YOUR ONE FILE: skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md. Touch nothing else except the tests you must keep green (you may not weaken a test — see below) and the census regeneration named at the end.

THE TASK, and its exact discipline. The file carries 211 findings: 101 sentences past the length cap, 110 style findings. Your job is to make the skill READ better, not weigh less. This is NOT truncation and NOT summarising.

For each finding from `python3 scripts/rule-census.py skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md` (run it to get the list with locations):
1. A sentence past the cap (over 25 words) becomes two or three short sentences. EVERY term, EVERY number, EVERY requirement, EVERY spec code of the original must survive. If the original said "within 10 minutes", the rewrite says it too. If it named three conditions, the rewrite names three.
2. A style finding is repaired by saying the thing positively in its own words. The commonest one here is the contrast frame ("X, not Y") — the repair is to state X as a claim that stands alone, not to delete Y's information. If Y carried a real exclusion the reader needs, keep it as its own sentence.
3. READ FIRST and follow: skills/text-audit/references/rewrite-meaning-check.md. It is the pack's own discipline for proving a rewrite kept its meaning — it lists the fields to check (actor, force, condition, scope, threshold, exception, output, side effect). Apply it to every place you touch. A rewrite that drops the actor or softens the force is a failure even if it reads nicely.

WHAT YOU MAY NOT DO:
- Do not delete a requirement, an example, a spec code, or a cross-reference to make a count fall.
- Do not move text into references/ — that is a different lane's technique and not authorised here.
- Do not weaken a test. Many phrases in this file are pinned by tests. Before rewriting a sentence, grep tests/ guardrails/ scripts/ for a distinctive fragment of it. If a phrase is pinned, EITHER keep that exact phrase intact inside your rewrite, OR leave the sentence alone and note it. Never edit the test to match your new wording.
- If a sentence cannot be split without losing meaning — a roster line, a list-bearing definition, a legal-style enumeration — LEAVE IT and record it with the reason. The brief expects such cases and wants them named, not forced.

PROOF, in this order:
1. `python3 scripts/rule-census.py skills/build-pipeline/SKILL.md` before and after — report both numbers. The count must fall substantially; it need not reach zero.
2. Every test that pins this file, green. Find them: `grep -rln "build-pipeline" tests/ | head -40`, then run exactly those.
3. `python3 guardrails/check-doc-findings-bound.py` green.
4. Regenerate the census record so the tree's numbers agree: `python3 scripts/rule-census.py --json guardrails/rule-census.json`, and commit it with your file.
5. `python3 scripts/gen-tree-counts.py` and commit README.md too if the line counts moved (this is the night's standing rule for any package that changes a skill's size).

Commit with explicit paths only, in coherent batches. Plain-words messages. End each with:
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Final report: findings before → after (both the long and the style halves); how many places you rewrote; the list of places you refused to touch, each with its reason; every phrase you had to keep verbatim because a test pins it; and the test results.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

# Checking that a rewrite still instructs the same thing

This file belongs to the `text-audit` skill, whose body is [`../SKILL.md`](../SKILL.md). The body's
loop asks whether a stranger understands a text. This file asks a second question of a rewrite: does
the new text still tell its reader to do the same thing?

Run these steps over any rewrite of text that binds someone. A skill body, a guardrail's printed
message, a spec criterion, an installed file, and a step a reader follows all bind someone.

Why the steps exist: a rewrite of eleven skill files dropped phrases the test suite required. Nobody
read the old and the new version side by side. The audit loop in the skill body reads how the new
text lands on a stranger. It reports nothing about the eight fields in step 1.

Every path below is relative to the root of the live-spec repository, which is the directory holding
`PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, `guardrails/`, and `scripts/`. A path opening with `references/` names a file in
this skill's own directory, beside this one.

## Step 1 — put each changed unit beside the version it replaces

Take the rewrite one unit at a time. A unit is one criterion, one paragraph, or one list item. Put it
beside the text it replaces, and answer all eight questions. Write each answer on its own line.

| Field | The question to answer |
|---|---|
| Actor | Does the same person or the same part of the system act? |
| Force | Do must, should, may, and any prohibition carry the same weight? |
| Condition | Does the rule apply under the same trigger? |
| Scope | Does it bind the same text, system, people, and stretch of time? |
| Threshold | Are the quantities, units, direction, and comparison unchanged? |
| Exception | Does every carve-out and every fallback survive? |
| Output | Are the names, formats, destinations, and generated files unchanged? |
| Side effect | Does the same action change the same state? |

A change made on purpose gets its own line under the field it moved. Keep those lines apart from the
readability findings, so whoever reads the record can tell the two apart.

## Step 2 — resolve every path and run every command the text teaches

- Open every path, link, and file name the changed text carries, and confirm each one resolves.
- Run every command the text teaches, from the working directory the text names.
- Carry out each taught step in a temporary directory, and read what it produced.
- Run the suite from the repository root: `python3 -m pytest -q`.

The suite pins exact phrases out of these documents, so a dropped phrase turns a test red. When a test
fails on a phrase, say which of three kinds that phrase is:

- the phrase carries the rule, so the rewrite changed the rule and the rewrite goes back;
- the phrase names something another file depends on, so both move in one change;
- the phrase is incidental wording, and the test may take the new words.

A test takes new words only in the third case.

## Step 3 — edit the source of a generated file, then regenerate

Find the source and the generator before touching anything. `scripts/gen-language-consumers.py` builds
four files out of `guardrails/language-rules.json`:

- `docs/language-rules.md`;
- `docs/language-rule-coverage.md`;
- `hooks/language-laws.json`;
- [`references/reader-prompt.md`](reader-prompt.md), and the rule block inside
  [`references/human-prose-rules.md`](human-prose-rules.md).

A hand edit to any of them turns `python3 guardrails/check-language-rules.py` red. Edit the source, run
the generator, and compare every one of those files against a fresh build.

To read a fresh build without writing into the tree, send the generator to a scratch directory:

```bash
out_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
python3 scripts/gen-language-consumers.py --out-dir "$out_dir"
```

`PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md` is generated the same way, by `python3 scripts/build-index.py PRODUCT_SPEC.md
-o PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md`. Its gate is `python3 guardrails/check-index-generated.py PRODUCT_SPEC.md
PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md`.

## Step 4 — install into a temporary home and compare

`install.sh` copies every directory under `skills/` into `$HOME/.claude/skills`. Point it at a
throwaway home, so a live copy on the machine stays untouched:

```bash
tmp_home="$(mktemp -d)"
HOME="$tmp_home" bash install.sh
diff -r skills/text-audit "$tmp_home/.claude/skills/text-audit"
```

The copy carries the reference files as well, so a reference the rewrite added shows up in the diff.

## Step 5 — report what a session pays to read the rewrite

Give the sizes separately, so whoever reads the report can see where the words went:

```bash
wc -c skills/text-audit/SKILL.md skills/text-audit/references/*.md
```

The frontmatter at the top of `SKILL.md` is indexed in every session. The body loads when the skill
loads. Each file under `references/` loads only for the task that needs it.

## Step 6 — hold the recorded finding count

`python3 scripts/rule-census.py` counts findings per file. It counts prose sentences past the 25-word
human-prose cap, plus the findings of `scripts/spec-style-lint.py`, plus the findings of
`scripts/preshow-register-lint.py`. `guardrails/rule-census.json` records the count each file is
allowed to carry.

`python3 guardrails/check-doc-findings-bound.py` refuses a push where a file stands above its recorded
count. A file recorded at zero reds on its first finding. A file the record has never heard of also
reds, so a new file is measured and recorded before it can pass.

## The texts that prove a step catches something

`evals/fixtures/text-audit/` holds three short texts, each carrying one known defect. The test
`tests/test_text_audit_fixtures.py` names the planted defect of each one, and it says which shipped
check reports that defect.

Hand `evals/fixtures/text-audit/rewrite-weakens-the-rule.md` to any worker that claims to verify a
rewrite. A worker that misses the changed actor, the softened force, or the dropped exception has
failed before it touches a real document.

1	---
2	name: build-pipeline
3	description: Use to run a non-trivial feature, bug fix, behavior change, refactor, docs-only change, or feature removal through the full spec-to-ship pipeline. Use it as well to set a project up on live-spec, where it reads the tree, picks the setup walk, and runs it. Spoken: attach live-spec to this project, adopt or install live-spec here, onboard this codebase onto live-spec, found a new project on live-spec, update live-spec here. A tiny reversible edit and pure research stay outside the pipeline.
4	metadata:
5	  version: 5.0.0
6	---
7	
8	# build-pipeline — ship a change by the method
9	
10	> Part of the **live-spec pack** — the shared working rules (ask-never-guess · plain words, anchors trail ·
11	> one surface = one name · one home per fact · junior/senior split · checkpoints · the concurrent-edit
12	> fence · freshness · journal discipline · attic-never-delete · verify by deed · the human's gates · claims
13	> need primary sources · fix the class, sweep look-alikes · the door before code · prototype ≠ product) live ONCE in the pack's base skill, `live-spec-base` (v5.0.0), together with the
14	> settings ladder — this skill references them and elaborates only its own domain. Used standalone, this
15	> note is plain advice.
16	
17	## Words this skill uses
18	
19	**Where the paths point.** Two repositories are in play. A path naming `skills/`, `guardrails/`,
20	`scripts/`, `templates/`, or `tests/` sits in the live-spec pack's own repository,
21	`github.com/happysasha18/live-spec`. An install copies each skill folder into one place, so a path
22	naming another skill points to that skill's folder, beside this skill's folder. A path opening with
23	`references/` names a file inside this skill's own directory, beside this file. Every other path
24	belongs to the project under change, including `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`,
25	`TEST_MATRIX.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `JOURNAL.md`, `docs/prover/`, and `.live-spec/`.
26	
27	- **the pack** — the shipped live-spec method: its skills, its document templates, and its gates.
28	  `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md` holds the shared rulebook and names the ten working skills.
29	- **host** — one project the pack attaches to. Each host holds its own spec, queue, journal, and
30	  `.live-spec/` folder.
31	- **the human** — the person who owns the product decisions. A taste call, a threshold, and a policy
32	  all reach them.
33	- **seat** — the orchestrating session that owns judgment, briefs workers, and reports to the human.
34	  This page also calls that actor the senior and the orchestrator.
35	- **worker** — a delegated session the seat briefs for bounded mechanical work, narrowed to the files
36	  its brief names. This page also calls it the junior.
37	- **wish** — one request as it was spoken, before the door places it.
38	- **door** — the intake classification that places a wish at one entry point: feature, bug, refactor,
39	  docs-only, or skip. It is decided before any code is written, and it stands apart from the wish's size.
40	- **work-kind** — the intake axis naming what a wish produces: product, infra, skill, or prose.
41	- **footprint** — the reach of one change: presentation-only, single-module, or cross-cutting.
42	- **tripwire** — one fixed rule in the door step that lifts a wish to a door whatever its casual label.
43	- **row** — one line of the project's queue, `ROADMAP.md` in this pack, holding one piece of work.
44	- **spec-delta**, also **the delta** — the set of spec sentences one wish adds or changes.
45	- **regression fence** — one sentence in a delta naming a neighbouring promise that must stay true,
46	  citing the existing clause it guards.
47	- **landing** — the act of one piece of work reaching the repository's shared truth as one commit.
48	- **lane**, also **train** — one build lane a session rolls through the pipeline.
49	- **the pen** — the single write-lock a repository holds. One lane at a time writes shared files under it.
50	- **departures board** — the status view read live off the queue's open rows. It names each rolling
51	  lane's step, and whom a waiting lane waits behind.
52	- **red**, used as a verb — a check fails and stops the work at that point. **Green** names a run with
53	  zero failures.
54	- **gate** — a check that must pass before the work proceeds.
55	- **architecture node** — one named unit in `ARCHITECTURE.md`. It carries one responsibility, owns the
56	  spec facts it implements, and pins them to the code.
57	- **seam** — the named boundary between two nodes, stating what crosses it and who owns the format.
58	- **checkpoint** — a saved point of work a session or a worker resumes from, written under `.live-spec/`.
59	- **norm** — an approved prototype frozen as the binding record of a surface's look and feel, kept
60	  under `docs/norms/`.
61	- **problem ledger** — the per-host file `.live-spec/PROBLEMS.md`, recording the workshop's recurring
62	  operational noise.
63	- **class hunt** — the search a confirmed bug drives before it closes. Name the defect abstractly,
64	  find every sibling of that kind, and fix them together.
65	- **compaction** — the station that removes redundancy from a document or from code.
66	- **shopfront** — the public README as the reader-facing front of a repository.
67	- **attic** — the host's append-only archive folder, `attic/`, where a superseded file moves.
68	
69	**The bracket codes.** `INV-`, `T-`, `E-`, `ACT-`, and `M-` codes index requirements in this pack's
70	own `PRODUCT_SPEC.md`. `PRODUCT_SPEC.index.md` maps each code to the criteria that carry it. The word
71	`SPEC` before a code marks that same home and names no separate series. `M-1` is the milestone gate
72	and `M-6` is the push gate. A **base rule N** points at the numbered rule N in
73	`skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md`; its own frontmatter states how many it carries. A **communicator rule N** points into
74	`skills/communicator/SKILL.md`. That file numbers twice: its behaviour rules carry an inline
75	`(rule N)` tag, and its writing-register checklist restarts at 1. This page names which of the two
76	it means each time.
77	Each sentence beside a code states its own
78	rule in full, so a reader holding this page alone can pass the codes over.
79	
80	## The pipeline in one line
81	
82	One pipeline, and steps 1, 2, 5, and 6 each invoke a named skill. The order is **spec → prove → architecture → prove architecture →
83	matrix → test → code → verify → commit & show**. A bug shortcuts to **bug → matrix → test → code** (citing the
84	existing architecture node it lands in). **Skip the pipeline only if ALL hold:** single
85	file · no new state / element / user-visible behaviour · an existing test level already covers the touched
86	fact (still ship a test; the order of test and fix follows test-author's small-fix path — red first by
87	default, and a one-batch fix owes the mechanical red proof). A skip still owes the door step's spec-backed-literal tripwire: does this edit touch a spec-backed literal or clause? A yes routes the docs and the test into the same session as the fix (SPEC INV-104). Anything touching visibility / layout / colour enters at the matrix step minimum.
88	Otherwise don't skip a step — the bugs that pass every test hide in the steps you skipped. (The private playbook repo's PLAYBOOK.md holds
89	the principle behind each step. This skill is its executable projection; keep the two in sync.)
90	
91	**The craft ladder — which craft's standards judge each step (SPEC INV-33).** Each artifact is judged by its
92	own craft's standards: **spec** — a strong product manager (the user's journey, the
93	product's words) · **prove / prove architecture** — the prover's formal-methods reviewer ·
94	**architecture** — a software architect (nodes, seams, one responsibility each) · **matrix** — a QA
95	automation lead deriving coverage · **test** — the same QA engineer writing it · **code** — a senior
96	developer · **verify** — the visitor's own fresh eyes, the builder's own view set aside · **commit & show** — a careful
97	release hand whose reader is the human.
98	
99	The delivery report's step accounting speaks in these standards. The craft each artifact was made under is
100	namable on ask.
101	
102	The craft takes the work-KIND's form (SPEC INV-22, INV-33): on a prose product the code step is worked as
103	a strong writer, on infra as a toolsmith. The ladder names the archetypes, and the kind says what their
104	standards look like in its medium.
105	
106	## When to run it — and where each kind of change enters
107	- **Step zero, before ANY tool call: name the door aloud (SPEC T-12, INV-16; base rule 15) — and the human hears the intake line back as the capture echo: heard · door · name · row · place on the map (communicator rule 12, its capture-echo behaviour rule; SPEC INV-27, INV-37).**
108	  - The intake line states size (a wish too big for its worth is negotiated in SCOPE — cut surfaces or
109	    split into stages, never a time budget or estimate; proposals proceed on the recommended option and
110	    are surfaced, SPEC T-15) · priority · door: feature · bug · refactor · docs-only · skip · work-kind: product · infra · skill ·
111	    prose — what the wish BUILDS, one kind per wish, scaling the FORM of every step it walks (the
112	    work-kind table at [references/work-kind-table.md](references/work-kind-table.md); SPEC T-16, INV-22).
113	
114	    The same line PLACES the wish on the product's feature map — **changes feature X · a new feature ·
115	    restructure** — spoken in the echo and written in the row's `map:` note. The map is the spec's scenario
116	    sections plus the architecture's nodes, never a third document. A restructure verdict queues its OWN row
117	    (refactor door if only structure moves, feature door if behaviour moves too); the re-carve happens only
118	    through the architecture step and its re-prove (SPEC INV-37). A same-version docs-layout pass rides one sanctioned light vehicle: the pass builds on a clean pushed base, locks the owner's decisions in a checkpoint first, and proves content survived by a word-token multiset check and a punctuation multiset check (SPEC INV-111).
119	  - **The same line reads the FOOTPRINT — a three-source impact read that decides the route (SPEC INV-128).**
120	    Beside the door and the work-kind, read the change against the spec, the architecture and the code at
121	    once, and name one footprint — **presentation-only** · **single-module** · **cross-cutting** — spoken in
122	    the echo and written in the row's `footprint:` note. See
123	    [references/footprint-read.md](references/footprint-read.md) for the full read: how the footprint
124	    composes with the door, what each footprint grants each step, what a three-source disagreement owes,
125	    and the mid-work re-classification.
126	  - Tripwires decide by rule, ahead of judgment — a new user-visible surface · new persistent state · a new interaction on an existing surface
127	    · the spec marks the touched surface [target] · behaviour no spec clause backs ⇒ FEATURE, however
128	    casually asked. The tripwire verdict outranks a casual "bugfix" label, and queue-cutting belongs to the
129	    bug door alone — a re-doored wish takes no preemption.
130	  - Re-fire the door mid-work the moment the work is
131	    about to create a surface or state its door doesn't grant: STOP, reclassify, continue by the right
132	    door. When the re-door creates a surface or state that did not exist when the lanes opened, the same
133	    re-check **re-runs the independence edges against every rolling lane (SPEC INV-131)** — the new surface
134	    can collide with a sibling that was independent a moment ago; a new edge pulls the re-doored lane back
135	    to serial (waiting behind the lane it now shares a surface with) with a board line, so the departures
136	    board never asserts a stale independence after the ground moved. The integration re-fence [INV-39]
137	    still catches the collision at landing; this closes the board's observability gap and adds no new net.
138	  - **A declared mockup-first entry condition is honoured from the row, cancelled only by name (SPEC
139	    INV-43).** See [references/mockup-first-entry.md](references/mockup-first-entry.md) for where the
140	    condition is written, what cancels it, and the worked case behind it.
141	  - **One wish = one user story (SPEC T-17):** a wish carrying several distinct things a person will DO and
142	    SEE splits at intake — each story its own row through the full pipeline (stages slice ONE story's depth,
143	    T-15's knife; separate stories never fuse into one row). Sub-behaviours (a hover face, a phone face, a
144	    backpointer) are the story's ACCEPTANCE, folded into the one story. Unclear whether it is one story or
145	    two ⇒ ask at intake, and every row born of a split cites the one spoken wish it came from. A request to
146	    merely SEE/TRY with no commitment goes to a labelled prototype home instead (base rule 16) — it stays a
147	    prototype, outside prod and unshown as product.
148	- **The door set is CLOSED, and a request enters at the highest document its change reaches (SPEC INV-151).** A request enters at the highest document in the derivation chain — spec → architecture → matrix → code → docs — whose sentences must change to satisfy it; the settings ladder stands beside the chain for a pure value. Walk the chain from the top: after this is done, would any sentence in this document read differently? The first yes is the entry layer, and the request flows down through every step its door grants. The set of entry points is closed — every request kind has a named home and a mandatory back-check, and a request the set cannot place is one plain question, never an improvised route:
149	
150	  See [references/request-kind-table.md](references/request-kind-table.md) for the full closed set of
151	  request kinds, their entry step, and mandatory back-check (product behaviour · a technically-phrased request · a defect · docs-only · a tiny reversible edit · a settings/parameter value · an inbox wish · a method/skill change · a sketch · research/a question · a feedback hand-back).
152	
153	  **A request that matches no kind in this closed set becomes one plain question to the human (base rule 1), never a guessed route.** The closed set is what makes "no gap between the layers" a checkable property held by rule, where before it leaned on habit: the landing contract already lists every door-granted step applied or stood down by name (SPEC INV-22), so a request the set cannot place is surfaced to the human as a question. This is the request-side twin of the property net's homeless-item finding (SPEC INV-150), the deferral test's (SPEC INV-152), and the earned message's (SPEC INV-189, INV-191) — one routing principle stated four times (SPEC INV-153): every incoming thing routes to the home whose declared sentence governs it, and a thing that pins to no home is itself the finding. The fourth control carries it across a window's edge: a message to another agent routes to the sender's own blocked work, and a question no work stands on is dropped and never sent.
154	- **New feature / new stateful surface / behaviour change:** the full pipeline from step 1.
155	- **Bug:** enter at the matrix step with a red-on-bug test (`bug → matrix → test → code`); if the fixed fact
156	  also lives in SPEC prose, update the spec sentence in the same change. **The door step adds one tripwire at the bug door:** does this edit touch a spec-backed literal or clause (a version string, a pinned count, a named vocabulary, a promised wording)? A yes binds the docs-travel-with-the-change rule and the red-first small-fix path into one duty — the docs and the test land in the same session as the fix; the tripwire reads the edit's content, so a one-word change to a spec-cited literal owes the same duty as a full feature (SPEC INV-104). **A confirmed bug drives a class hunt before it closes (SPEC INV-124). The hunt is four moves:** (1) name the defect abstractly (the KIND of mistake — a scope too narrow, a
157	  missing guard, an assumption that holds in one place and fails in the neighbour), then actively SEARCH
158	  every surface where that kind could live and fix all siblings in the same change — the search goes
159	  finding the siblings not yet seen, the matrix row and the red-on-bug test covering the CLASS beyond the
160	  single instance (base rule 14); (2) check the architecture — a structural cause (a boundary drawn wrong
161	  or left silent, a node owning what it should not) updates ARCHITECTURE.md in the same change, a cluster
162	  in one district reading as an architecture smell; (3) check the spec — a spec silent on or
163	  under-describing the broken behaviour is the real defect, fixed FIRST so the prover can flag it, then
164	  the code fix lands under it (the spec-under-describes-composition lesson, generalized); (4) escalate to
165	  the human when the class boundary needs his read — which behaviours are one class, what the intended
166	  design was, whether a whole area wants a rethink — the method stops and asks for the boundary, and does not guess it. The four moves are the bug door's close condition; a point fix that leaves the siblings
167	  standing is a status, never a landing (SPEC INV-26). **A RECURRING bug re-doors to feature:**
168	  a second bug in the same area within ~30 days is not another patch — the area is missing an INVARIANT,
169	  so it escalates to the full pipeline from step 1 (spec the invariant, re-prove, then fix under it).
170	  The journal is how you notice: before taking any bug, grep JOURNAL.md for the area's name and check
171	  the dates.
172	- **Removal of a shipped feature is a change too:** spec section → dated REMOVED tombstone · matrix rows
173	  retired (not left "BUILT") · owning tests deleted · SKILL.md / README swept — all the same session. (This
174	  is the step that actually got skipped once: an excision cleaned code + tests but left four doc surfaces dangling.)
175	- **Refactor (behaviour-neutral):** no spec/matrix delta, but enter at step 8 with the FULL suite + the
176	  visual sample set + a matrix audit of the touched sections (a monolith refactor re-risks everything);
177	  if the refactor moves node boundaries but leaves the document's shape standing, ARCHITECTURE.md's pins
178	  update in the same change — the pins-only path is scoped to a boundary shift that leaves the document's
179	  shape standing. A deliberate redesign (layers restacked, a surface's ownership moved, nodes merged or
180	  split) re-shapes the architecture document to the new form and re-proves it with the architecture lens
181	  in the same movement (SPEC INV-113); updating the pins alone does not cover a redesign.
182	- **Docs-only change:** re-read the changed section rendered + one grep that no stale claim contradicts the
183	  code; no spec/matrix step.
184	- **A rewrite or restyle accounts for every removal of substance (SPEC INV-109):** the rule's one home is communicator rule 6, the removal-accounting step of that skill's writing-register checklist, which owns the delivery report the accounting rides. The docs-only door above and the restyle loop both invoke it — every removed section, argument, rationale, or worked example listed there with its one line of judgment, a removal the rewriter cannot justify raised as a question before the report closes, line-level wording left free.
185	- **A restructure or migration merged back to main is gated on the delta (SPEC INV-114):** A restructure or migration merge gate judges the delta. It has three parts: load-bearing token identity old-versus-new modulo the per-chunk named deltas plus the punctuation-multiset check (SPEC INV-111); the full suite green on the merged tree (SPEC INV-39); and a full prover pass on both sides whose blocking set is delta-scoped — an unmatched token, a red suite, a new-side finding absent on the old side, or an unnamed meaning change. Pre-existing findings equal on both sides route to queue rows in the same landing and never block. And a session that sharpens a human's spoken bar beyond his words says the sharpened form back and marks it as its own interpretation. The token-identity part scopes to a content-preserving restructure. A deliberate redesign changes content by intent, so it routes by the architecture-redesign law (SPEC INV-113), and its merge stands on the green suite and the delta-scoped prover pass, with no token-identity demand over text the redesign meant to change.
186	- **Skip entirely** only under the single boundary above (pure research, fact-gathering, a one-file
187	  no-new-behaviour edit already covered by a test level).
188	
189	## Work that belongs elsewhere
190	
191	Skip it for the skip-boundary edit (single file · no new state, element, or visible behaviour · an existing
192	test level already covers the touched fact — it still ships a test, just no pipeline); not for pure
193	research or fact-gathering (no artifact changes); not for a SEE/TRY ask (that goes to the labelled
194	prototype home, base rule 16 — and comes BACK through this pipeline only at promotion).
195	
196	## Setting a project up on the pack
197	
198	A session that hears "attach live-spec to this project", "found a new project on live-spec", or
199	"update live-spec here" runs a setup walk first. Read
200	[references/project-setup.md](references/project-setup.md), the routing card beside this page. It
201	resolves the pack tree, reads the project tree, and names the walk this project takes. The setup
202	entry stands outside the derivation chain, beside the sketch lane. When the walk finishes, the first wish enters at its
203	own door like any other request.
204	
205	## The work-kind table — WHAT the wish builds scales HOW each step runs (SPEC T-16, INV-22)
206	
207	The door picks WHICH steps run. The kind picks the FORM each running step takes. The work-kind table
208	at [references/work-kind-table.md](references/work-kind-table.md) is the per-kind meanings' one
209	normative home. That is the one place they are stated, and the spec binds the contract around it. The
210	contract, before the table: at landing, every door-granted step has either **APPLIED in its kind's form
211	or STOOD DOWN by name** in the delivery report ("design-sync — text product, stands down") — a silently
212	skipped step is a defect. **An unresolved kind scales nothing down** — standing a step down requires a
213	NAMED kind (the ask rides the row, SPEC INV-12). And no kind ever touches the safety net: the door law
214	and its tripwires, the delta's mandatory sentences (fences · facets · non-goals · success measure),
215	ask-at-intake — the same law a scope cut obeys (SPEC T-15).
216	
217	See [references/work-kind-table.md](references/work-kind-table.md) for the full table of how each step
218	(1 spec · 2 prove · 3 architecture · 4 prove architecture · 5 matrix · 6 test · 7 code · 8 verify by deed · 9 commit & show · design-sync/snapshot) takes shape under product / infra / skill / prose, including the verify-by-deed VISITOR WALK and FEEL pass (SPEC INV-30, INV-136, INV-139) and the skill-review duty (SPEC INV-99).
219	
220	## The steps
221

452	## Guardrails — the pipeline's mechanical enforcement (every project inherits them)
453	The nine steps are guidance, and an agent drifts from guidance — that is the failure that stops a project
454	converging (a whole panel ships empty; a behaviour nobody asked for gets buried; a change lands with no test).
455	So the pipeline is not trusted, it is ENFORCED: a `guardrails` check the project wires to a **git pre-push
456	hook** (+ the suite), so a change that fails ANY of these is RED and CANNOT be pushed. `guardrails/` is a
457	directory of check scripts, and the pack ships one runner, `guardrails/pre-push`, that a project installs
458	as its own `.git/hooks/pre-push`. `tests/test_traceability.py`
459	(below) is the first of these — generalise it to the full set. **Each project INSTANTIATES the checks for its
460	own surfaces; the pipeline REQUIRES the check exists and is green.** This is a first-class step, applied across the whole project as a standing part of the method;
461	a per-project patch does not satisfy it. See
462	[references/guardrails-catalog.md](references/guardrails-catalog.md) for the four mechanical guardrails
463	(Completeness incl. cross-surface policy uniformity SPEC INV-125 · Tests-present · Behaviour-traces-to-spec ·
464	Conflicts).
465	**Honest boundary:** guardrails catch STRUCTURAL defects (empty surface, missing test, untraced behaviour,
466	partial artifact, id/naming conflict). They do NOT catch a subtle SEMANTIC bug (is the number right?) — that
467	still needs `product-prover` + a human's eyes. Enforce structure mechanically, and reason about meaning with
468	the prover. Verify-by-deed (step 8) and commit/push (step 9) both run the guardrails first, so guidance and
469	enforcement agree.

493	  stations run at every push, above the MINOR gate that once held them alone. Every push is held to the
494	  reached-clean floor by the mechanical gates — the register lint at zero errors, the redundancy gate at
495	  zero open pairs, and the debt cap that only ratchets down (`scripts/spec-debt-cap.json`) — asserted
496	  against the live document by the suite, so no bloat accumulates between milestones. This is the
497	  fix for the spec bloating when compaction ran milestone-only (2026-07-15).
498	- **Process bookkeeping scales to the delta (SPEC INV-61):** the pre-push re-check keeps its rigor and
499	  scales its FORM — a small delta (skill/prose/infra kind, no new surface, no structure change) ships a

502	  chapter and the resume rewrite come once per landing batch. Never scaled: the law's own text, the
503	  red-first test, the delta's prove, the gates.
504	- **Order is law:** `spec → prove → architecture → prove architecture → matrix → test → code`;
505	  `bug → matrix → test → code`. Never code first and back-fill a spec — and never jump from spec straight
506	  to tests: the two layers between them (architecture, test-spec derivation) are where whole classes of

511	  supersession, never compresses it away (still open at compaction ⇒ restated in full).

526	- **A worker never restores a working tree with a git command (SPEC INV-298; the gate INV-299).** Every
527	  brief this skill composes carries this clause verbatim. Before a worker mutates a file it means to put
528	  back, it reads that file and holds its bytes. A worker puts a file back by WRITING ITS OWN SAVED BYTES.
529	  A worker runs no command that discards uncommitted work, in any tree: `git checkout -- <path>`,
530	  `git checkout .`, `git restore` outside `--staged`, `git stash` and its `push`, `save`, `create` and
531	  `store` forms, `git reset` with `--hard`, `--merge` or `--keep`, and `git clean` with `-f` or `-x`. Such
532	  a command's blast radius is a PATH, so its damage lands on files the worker never wrote and its brief
533	  never named. This rule binds a worker in every tree, including its own isolated worktree, since a
534	  worktree shares one repository with the lanes beside it and a worker cannot read off its brief what else
535	  that repository holds. A worker that holds no saved bytes for a file it mutated, or that believes a file
536	  needs a git-level restore, HALTS and reports the file and the mutation it made, and it writes no further
537	  file and runs no further command. The orchestrator owns recovery: it restores the named file from the
538	  last committed stage, hands the worker a fresh brief carrying that file's current bytes, and records the
539	  halt in the row's delivery report, and the halted work resumes under that new brief. The orchestrator's
540	  own half: a finished build stage is committed before the next worker touches its files.
541	  `guardrails/check-worker-restore.py` reads the worker runs' transcripts for the command and runs at the
542	  verify step.
543	- **Traceability is a test, enforced automatically.** A standing `tests/test_traceability.py` fails the suite on a matrix row
544	  citing a missing test, a duplicate invariant id, a spec invariant with no matrix row, or a ⟨DECIDE⟩ marked
545	  RESOLVED that still carries the live marker — so drift is caught every commit, continuously, and never waits for the next MINOR.
546	
547	## How it relates to the other skills
548	- `spec-author` — writes/grows the spec (step 1). Public.
549	- `product-prover` — reviews the whole spec with formal-verification thinking (step 2). External skill, installed by `scripts/install-external-skills.sh`; pack bindings in `skills/product-prover-pack/SKILL.md`.
550	- `design-reviewer` — a second pass right after the prover (step 2): judges the design, proposes the
551	  same-kind groupings the text never declared, and echoes the strongest likely divergence to the human;
552	  recommendations and questions only, never a block. Public.
553	- `test-author` — derives the matrix and writes the tests (steps 5–6). Public.
554	- `build-pipeline` (this) — the orchestrator that sequences them through to a shipped, verified, committed
555	  change.
556	
557	The pack holds six more skills, and `skills/live-spec-base/SKILL.md` names the ten working ones:
558	
559	- `live-spec-base` — the shared rulebook and the settings ladder. Every `base rule N` on this page
560	  points there.
561	- `communicator` — carries the work to the human. Every `communicator rule N` on this page points there.
562	- `publish` — runs the checks a publication owes its reader, invoked at step 9's shopfront walk.
563	- `text-audit` — reads a text as a stranger and repairs where they stop.
564	- `feedback-intake` — files what comes back from a person or an inbox.
565	- `feedback-collector` — offers a rare private note up to the pack's authors.
566	
567	> The method, made durable: spec-author and product-prover each own one step; build-pipeline is the spine that
568	> runs the whole arc from a spec to a shipped, tested, committed change.
569
